notes: Exact agreement is required only where the quantile sketch retains the raw order statistics. Elsewhere the two routes are bounded by the grid interval that brackets the observation, which is a property of monotone piecewise-linear interpolation rather than a chosen tolerance.

The residual interior difference is mostly definitional: the stored grid holds R type-7 quantiles while both tail estimates use Weibull plotting positions. The two disagree by roughly one order statistic.

suites.title: Missing-data handling
suites.description: Every form of absent or insufficient input produces a named exclusion or no candidate at all — never a score that looks as though the data were present.

metrics.detail: below_score_threshold, dry_day_not_ranked, insufficient_baseline, insufficient_wet_days, no_baseline

metrics.detail: must be 0

metrics.label: Completeness floor
metrics.detail: a run under this refuses to publish

cases.title: A completely ordinary day, which must not reach the board
cases.detail: The single most important negative case in the set. A median day scores about 0.30, under the 0.5 publication floor, so the ranking is not merely ordering noise on quiet days — it declines to publish it.

cases.title: A dry day is not an upper-tail event
cases.detail: Dry spells are a multi-day question and out of scope for a daily metric, so zero rainfall is excluded by name rather than scored as a lower-tail outlier.

cases.title: No cached baseline for this city, metric and day
cases.detail: Must produce an inspectable exclusion, not a silent drop and not a score computed against nothing.

cases.title: Baseline row exists but its sample is empty
Too few reference values to estimate a tail
cases.detail: 100 < the 120-sample floor. The value would score highly if scored, which is exactly why the gate has to come first.

cases.title: Enough values, drawn from too few years
cases.detail: Sample count alone is not enough: 450 values from 10 years cannot resolve a 1-in-30-year tail, however many of them there are.

cases.title: Almost no wet days in the reference window
cases.detail: Expects 'insufficient_baseline' rather than 'insufficient_wet_days' on purpose. The baseline builder folds the wet-day floor into the 'sufficient' flag, so that broader gate fires first. Recorded as observed behaviour, not asserted as the nicer of the two names.

cases.title: Wet-day floor raised above the value used when the baseline was built
cases.detail: The only route by which 'insufficient_wet_days' is reachable, and the reason it is still worth having: a caller that demands a stricter floor than the stored baseline was built to must be refused rather than served.

cases.title: Observation absent
cases.detail: Nothing to score, so nothing is returned — as distinct from a baseline problem, which produces a named exclusion.

cases.title: Observation is NaN
cases.detail: A NaN that reached the scorer would propagate through every comparison and silently sort anywhere, so it has to be refused at the door.

cases.title: Scores just under the publication floor
An excluded candidate still carries the evidence for why
cases.expected: evidence contains the exclusion reason and the baseline it was judged against
cases.detail: Exclusions are dropped from the board but not from the record. Without this, 'my city is missing' has no answer.

cases.title: Served methodology version matches the code

limitations: Every figure in this report was measured by the run that produced it. Nothing is hardcoded; a suite that cannot measure something reports null.

The pipeline, API and published-explanation checks run against 'synthetic_fixture_v1', a deterministic synthetic weather provider. They measure whether the machinery is correct and reproducible, not the accuracy of real weather data.
Latency figures come from an in-process client over an in-memory SQLite database. They are a floor for the deployed system, not a measurement of it.

The anomaly-score evaluator compares production against independent arithmetic in two regimes. Where the observation sits at or beyond the fifth order statistic from either end the stored quantile sketch is lossless and exact agreement is required. In the interior the sketch interpolates across its probability grid, so the two are only required to agree within the width of the grid interval that brackets the observation — a property of the interpolation, not a tolerance chosen to make the run pass. The measured worst case is reported either way.
Grounding accuracy is measured on a small hand-labelled case set. It quantifies the guards, not any language model's general reliability.
LLM spend is an estimate derived from configured token prices. When no prices are configured it reads 0.0, which means 'not priced' rather than 'free'.

The city registry is a curated sample of major North American cities. It is not a representative sample of the continent's climate, and the rankings are statistical outliers within that sample rather than records of any kind.
